ones: a mature $400k token with cluster activity becomes an EARLY-STAGE

_note: Requirements shared by BOTH insider tiers. Enforced in audit.mjs by
evaluateInsiderRequirements(), which is stricter than the contract
audit in one specific way: UNKNOWN COUNTS AS FAILURE. The contract
audit reports missing provider data as UNVERIFIED and leaves the token
watchable; an insider tier is a promotion — a louder header, and score
for the established tier — so it may not rest on data that was never
returned.
Mint/freeze revoked and 'audit must be PASSED' are implicit in those
two rows and are not separately configurable: they are the definition
of a clean contract, not a tunable.

floor is part of the tier definition, not just a Telegram setting.
The score cannot be checked during classification — the tier's own
scoreBoost feeds into it — so the floor is applied at dispatch.

_note: Community Takeover detection — the $RAVECAT pattern: developer walks
away, the crowd keeps trading, and the token survives without them.
All four criteria must pass. None is meaningful alone: holders can be
sybilled, volume can be washed, and a dev can move funds to a second
wallet and look 'exited'. Together they are decent evidence, and they
are treated as evidence rather than proof.
maxDevBalancePct is read from chain (the creator's live token balance as
a share of supply), NOT from a provider flag, and only after the three
free criteria pass — so the extra RPC call costs nothing on tokens that
were never candidates. An unreadable balance FAILS the criterion: 'we
could not find the dev's balance' is not 'the dev has gone'.
WHAT A CONFIRMED CTO OVERRIDES: the dev-exit penalty (creator-sold risk
flags stop counting, since a departed dev is the premise) and the
liquidity depth RATIO, replaced by the $100k absolute floor in
thresholds.minAbsoluteLiquidityUsd.
WHAT IT NEVER OVERRIDES: mint authority, freeze authority, LP burn,
top-10 concentration, the 150-holder floor, or a SERIAL RUGGER deployer.
A crowd cannot revoke an authority the developer kept, and 'the
community took it over' is exactly the story that would be told to
launder a rugger's token.
Three pillars, adapted from the equities cluster-buying idea. The
adaptation is weaker by nature: equities insiders are named in mandatory
filings, on-chain ones are inferred from behaviour.
PILLAR 1 cluster   — 2+ tracked or co-funded wallets buying inside the
launch window. One buyer is noise; several together
within seconds is coordination.
PILLAR 2 sizing    — a single buy over 5 SOL or over 5% of the pool.
Size cannot be faked.
PILLAR 3 funder    — wallets whose FIRST funding shares a source. Verified
working against Helius: a fresh wallet's earliest
transaction reveals both funder and amount.
LIMITS: funder tracing only reaches wallets with <1000 lifetime
signatures (RPC page limit), which excludes established traders — fine,
since cabal wallets are purpose-made and fresh. A shared funder is often
just a CEX hot wallet, so it is reported but scored only lightly and
never treated as proof of insider knowledge.
_scalingNote: Multi-insider scaling multiplier, keyed on the count of DISTINCT insider
wallets. The three detection sources overlap heavily — one wallet can be
watchlisted AND early AND co-funded — so the count is of unique addresses,
not list lengths, or a single wallet would score as three.
Applied ONLY after every safety gate passes. audit.mjs zeroes this on any
gate failure, so a cabal buying its own rug can never outscore a clean
ADDITIVE to the fundamentals, not a floor: a swarm lands at base+50
clamped to 100. A token with weak demand and thin liquidity will not
reach 90 on insider count alone — four wallets buying something illiquid
is a reason to look, not a reason to override the market data.

_note: DexScreener has no trending endpoint (403/404 on every variant). The
boost/profile feeds skew tiny — measured 0 pairs above $1M. The search
endpoint skews the opposite way, so both are used and unioned.
Measured yield per query into the $300k-$8M band: solana=13, SOL=4,
dog=2, pump/cat/AI/trump=1 each, meme/moon/WIF=0.
Guards against system accounts masquerading as whales.
maxWalletSol catches exchange vaults (one held 10.7M SOL).
maxTokenAccounts catches DEX pool authorities, which hold trivial SOL
but own millions of token accounts — Raydium Authority V4 owns 1,416,453.
A balance check alone would wave those straight through.
Composite Elite Ranking. All three rules must pass — they are AND, not a
weighted blend, so a small-sample 100% win rate cannot buy a place.
No provider serves the ranking data: GMGN 403s behind Cloudflare, Birdeye
and Dune 401 without a paid key, Cielo's public feed is empty, Solscan
refuses connections. So the list is EARNED from Aegis's own observations
(buyer replay + post-mortem grading) rather than fetched. Seed it instantly
with:  node auto_top_whales.mjs --import <leaderboard.csv>
syncIntervalHours = 2: re-ranks win rates and rewrites smart_wallets.json
every 2h during the normal 12-minute scan. The ledger itself updates on
EVERY scan (buys recorded, outcomes graded) — this interval only controls
how often the ranking is recomputed and the watchlist file rewritten.
_option2Note: Top-5 Earned Whales. minGradedBuys lowered 10 -> 3 because the ledger
showed 0 wallets could ever reach 10: a wallet cannot hold more graded
buys than there are decided tokens, and recurrence collapses 3-4x per
level (1466 wallets at >=1, 36 at >=2, 9 at >=3, 2 at >=5).
profitRule is 'skip' because nothing writes otherwise — lifetime realized
P&L is not derivable from observation. Ranking is therefore on win rate +
on-chain activity only. Imported leaderboards still carry real P&L.
SAMPLE-SIZE WARNING: at minGradedBuys=3 with a 75% win-rate bar, a wallet
with exactly 3 graded buys must be 3/3 perfect (2/3 = 66.7% fails). So the
first entries are near-perfect records over very few trades. Treat these
as candidates to watch, not proven edge, until their graded counts grow.

_insiderTiersOnlyNote: Restricts alerts to the two named tiers, so every notification carries
one of the two headers and a market-cap band you chose deliberately.
KNOWN GAP, stated rather than hidden: the tiers do not cover $12k-$30k
or $500k-$1M. An insider-backed token in either of those windows now
scores and writes a note as before but sends NO Telegram alert, where
previously it would have. Set this to false to restore alerts on every
insider-detected token regardless of band, or widen insiderEarly's
maxMarketCapUsd to 1000000 to close the upper gap.
_insiderMinScoreNote: Set to 68 on 2026-08-08 after measuring against the overnight run.
Of the 10 alerts sent that night, 5 clear 68 (scores 68-76) and 5 fall
below (45-67). A 75 floor left only 1. 68 targets ~3-5 alerts/day.
Raise toward 75 for near-silence, lower toward 60 to roughly double flow.
_silenceNote: insiderOnly=true: Telegram receives a message ONLY when a token has
insider/cluster activity AND clears every safety gate. No digests, no
scam lists, no empty-scan summaries — a tick that finds nothing sends
This REPLACES the old BUY SIGNAL + minScore rule rather than adding to
it. Real insider entries frequently sit at WATCH because the 5m demand
ratio is under 2x at the moment of entry; requiring both would filter
out exactly the early buys this mode exists to catch.
sendScanDigest forced to false — it was the only remaining source of
routine noise. Set insiderOnly=false to restore the previous behaviour.

_note: What each named source actually contributes:
Solscan  — API is key-gated, so origin tracing runs against Solana RPC
directly (same data, no key). Solscan is used for links.
Bubblemaps — no public API. Its graph is reproducible from chain:
wallets sharing a funding origin. That is computed here.
GMGN     — 403 Cloudflare. Win rate / PnL / trade count CANNOT be
Birdeye  — 401 without a paid key.      fetched. Verified repeatedly.
So discovered wallets carry deep links to GMGN and Birdeye rather than
fabricated stats. Tap through for the numbers.
EXPANSION SAFETY — maxFunderDegree is the important one. A CEX hot wallet
funds thousands of unrelated users; without this guard the net would
enrol half of Solana in a day and every token would 'match smart money'.
Expansion also only proceeds from a cluster already containing a tracked
wallet, and results go to discovered_wallets.json — NOT smart_wallets.json,
which auto_top_whales.mjs rewrites wholesale every 2h and would erase.
Positions open when a BUY alert is delivered, capturing the market cap at
that moment and each insider's token balance. Those baselines are what the
triggers measure against.
Each trigger fires AT MOST ONCE per position — otherwise a token sitting
at -21% would re-send a stop-loss every 30 seconds.
STOP_LOSS and INSIDER_EXIT close the position. TAKE_PROFIT does NOT: its
advice is to remove initial capital and let the rest run, so the stop-loss
must stay armed on the remainder.
A delisted pair counts as a stop-loss, not missing data. Liquidity being
pulled is the most important thing to be told about.
IMPORTANT: percentages are movement from the ALERT market cap, not your
P&L. Aegis does not know your fill, your size, or whether you took the
trade at all.
_stopLossByCategoryNote: Resolves a contradiction shipped on 2026-08-08: the early-tier advice
text says 'enforce tight -15% stop-loss' while stopLossPct was a global
20, so the alert asked for a tighter stop than the notifier would send.
The category is captured on the position when the BUY alert fires, so a
position keeps the stop it was opened under even if this config changes
underneath it. Anything not listed here uses stopLossPct.
_takeProfitNote: Lowered 2.0 -> 1.5 on 2026-08-08 from measured behaviour, not preference.
Across 10 overnight positions: 8 hit STOP_LOSS, 0 hit TAKE_PROFIT, median
peak +56%. Five peaked between +56% and +99% and then round-tripped past
-20%. $NEEGY peaked at +99% — one point short of the 2x trigger.
At 1.5x those same five fire near their highs: 5/10 instead of 0/10.

_note: Channel listener (telegram_listener.mjs). Reads public signal channels
over MTProto and feeds any Solana mint it sees into the ordinary audit
pipeline.
SECURITY MODEL: channel text is DATA, never instruction. The listener
extracts base58 mints with a regex and discards everything else — it
does not follow links, act on commands, or trust any claim a channel
makes about a token. Every address goes through the same audit, shield
and insider pipeline as a discovered one, so a channel posting a rug
gets the rug verdict, not an alert.
requiresLogin: MTProto needs a USER session, not a bot token — bots
cannot read channels they do not administer. Run 'node
telegram_listener.mjs --login' yourself to produce a session string;
it asks for your phone, an SMS code and your 2FA password. Nobody else
should ever run that for you, and the session string it prints grants
full access to your Telegram account — treat it like a password.
channels: @usernames, t.me links or numeric ids. An empty list means
the listener watches every chat the session can see, which is noisy;
name the channels you actually want.
Cadence for loop.mjs. 30s is the TARGET, not the achieved rate: a full
pass measured 40-55s, and discovery is a fixed cost that does not shrink
with scanLimit. The loop skips a tick when the previous scan is still
running, so the real cadence tracks scan duration and skipped ticks are
reported rather than hidden.
To get closer to 30s: lower scanLimit and trim discovery.searchQueries.
RPC BUDGET: this runs ~2000 scans/day vs ~120 on the 12-minute task.
